choices.term: ἠδίκησα τοῦ μὴ ἀκοῦσαι, ἐσπού- δασα τοῦ μὴ βλέπειν.
choices.english: I have sinned by failing to listen, I have rushed ahead by refusing to look.
choices.why: The aorist ἠδίκησα and ἐσπούδασα convey completed self-reproach; μὴ with infinitive expresses the omitted action as the cause of fault. 'Failing to listen' and 'refusing to look' capture the volitional neglect better than literal 'not hearing/not seeing' which would imply mere absence of perception.
rejected: I have done wrong by not hearing, I have hurried by not seeing.

choices.term: Ἡ καρδία μου πλανᾶται, καὶ ἡ ἀνομία με βαπτίζει, ἡ ψυχή μου ἐφέστηκεν εἰς φόβον.
choices.english: My heart drifts astray, and lawlessness washes over me like a baptism, my soul has risen up into terror.
choices.why: Πλανᾶται is middle/passive suggesting drifting, not active wandering; βαπτίζει metaphorically means 'overwhelms' as in a ritual washing, not literal baptism; ἐφέστηκεν εἰς φόβον conveys a sudden rising into fear, not merely 'has risen into fear' which lacks the inceptive force. The metaphor of baptism for overwhelming sin is retained but rendered in natural English.
rejected: My heart wanders, and lawlessness baptizes me, my soul has risen into fear.

choices.term: Εἰσκομίζεται γὰρ ὁ Ἀσσύριος, καὶ δεδιὼς τὴν ἔφ-οδον, καὶ τῶν πολεμίων τὰς φάλαγγας οὐκ ἠγνοηκὼς, καὶ ἐπὶ τίνας αὐταῖς ὁ τοῦ πολέμου σκοπός.
choices.english: For the Assyrian enters, and fearing the road, and not having ignored the enemy's phalanxes, and upon which of them the aim of the war.
choices.why: The text is syntactically broken after 'upon which of them'; the participle δεδιὼς and perfect οὐκ ἠγνοηκὼς are causal/adverbial, not sequential. 'Fearing the road' renders δεδιὼς τὴν ὁδόν as the cause of entry. The final clause is left as a fragment per source, with σκοπός understood as 'aim' or 'target' of war. No completion is attempted.
rejected: For the Assyrian enters, fearing the way, and having not ignored the phalanxes of the enemies, and upon them the aim of the war.

choices.term: Τοῖς γὰρ ἐν ἐσχάτῃ συμφορᾷ γεγονόσι δοκεῖ προσεῖναί τις παραμυθίας τρόπος, τὸ θρηνεῖν τε καὶ ὀλοφύρεσθαι.
choices.english: For those who have come to pass in extreme misfortune seem to need a way of consolation, to lament and to wail.
choices.why: Προσεῖναί τις is impersonal 'it seems one needs'; θρηνεῖν τε καὶ ὀλοφύρεσθai is hendiadys for loud mourning. 'Come to pass' renders γεγονόσι as 'have come to be' in a state. The structure avoids the Greek word order while preserving the claim that extreme suffering naturally seeks expression in lament.
rejected: For those in extreme misfortune having come to be, it seems one needs a way of consolation, to lament and to wail.

choices.term: Πρᾶγμα δὲ ξένον εἰ θρη- νοῦσιν Ἀσσύριοι, σκληροὶ καὶ ἀγέρωχοι γεγονότες ἀεὶ, ἐξοφρυωμένοι τε ἅγαν κατὰ πάντων τῶν ἐθνῶν, καὶ οὐκ εὐάντητον ἔχειν οἰόμενοι τὴν ἀντίστασιν.
choices.english: But a thing strange if Assyrians lament, hardened and unfeeling having become always, swollen with pride against all nations, and thinking to possess not an easy resistance.
choices.why: The conditional εἰ θρηνοῦσιν is rendered as 'if Assyrians lament' to maintain the hypothetical force. Participles σκληροὶ... γεγονότες and ἐξοφρυωμένοι are causal: their hardness and pride are why lament would be strange. Οὐκ εὐάντητον ἔχειν is rendered 'thinking to possess not an easy resistance' to preserve the negation and their mistaken belief. No words are added.
rejected: But a thing strange if Assyrians lament, hardened and unfeeling having become always, swollen with pride against all nations, and thinking they do not possess an easy resistance.

choices.term: Ἀλλ' οἱ θρασεῖς οὕτω καὶ φρονήμασι τοῖς ὑπὲρ ἄνθρωπον ἐξογκούμενοι, γυναικοπρεπὲς εἰσδέχονται τὸ δάκρυον, καὶ θρῆνον ἐφ' ἑαυτοῖς ἀρτύουσι, πρὸ τῆς τοῦ πολέ- μου πείρας κατακλώμενοι πρὸς ἀσθένειαν.
choices.english: But the bold thus and in their thoughts exceeding man, receive the tear as womanly, and they accomplish lamentation upon themselves, before the trial of the war bending toward weakness.
choices.why: Ὑπὲρ ἄνθρωπον ἐξογκούμενοι is rendered 'exceeding man' to avoid the awkward 'exceeding human'; γυναικοπρεπὲς εἰσδέχονται is metaphorically 'receive the tear as womanly' to convey the perceived effeminacy. Ἐφ' ἑαυτοῖς ἀρτύουσι is 'accomplish lamentation upon themselves' to keep the reflexive force. Πρὸ τῆς... πείρας κατακλώμενοι πρὸς ἀσθένειαν is rendered as a participial clause 'bending toward weakness' to avoid the Greek absolute construction while preserving the meaning that they weaken themselves before war's trial.
rejected: But the bold thus and in their thoughts exceeding man, receive the tear as womanly, and they accomplish lamentation upon themselves, before the trial of the war bending toward weakness.

They will go through and pass through the wilderness. Like a storm of winds through a desert it passes. The dust rising up and confusing everything. He adds: That the sight is fearful and harsh was reported to me. For it is very bare and naked and alone among the enemies, the spectacle, and the most warlike multitude equipped for battle, to instill dread in the beholders. But he says not only to see, but also, 'It was reported to me,' he says. For together with the sight, and the outcome of the things, he taught, and it is clear that it is from God. 'The one who rejects rejects, and the one who transgresses transgresses.' He says, 'The arrogance of the coming things is unfillable.' For not by human calculations are they kindled for the day; nor does anyone among them reflect on anything of the coming things. But he transgresses without restraint, and rejects according to what seems to him, without any pity. For they do not look for mercy, but their work is what they have devoted themselves to, he says, to transgress and to reject. He spoke something like this also by the voice of the same, to the inhabitants of Assyria: Behold, I am bringing upon you the Medes, who do not value silver, nor do they have need of gold. The arrows of young men will shatter. For God's wrath being brought upon the sinners, nothing will be able to help. And the mind becomes like a beast of prey for those who wish to ravage whatever they run upon. Upon me are the Elamites, and the envoys of the Persians come to me. Now I will groan and exhort myself. Therefore my loins have been filled with dissolution, and pains have taken hold of me, like a woman in childbirth.
